description: Sizing-object artifact — the first-class routing artifact for the fleet routing lobby. Captures the PM's verbatim intent, the Shape-Up-style appetite BUDGET, a coarse provisional t-shirt routing estimate, and which room (dispatch/shape/plan/roadmap) the work should enter. Per-repo session-produced routing state, same taxonomy class as state/handoffs/ — see docs/wiki/state-placement-law.md § Taxonomy. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-24-sizing-lobby-core.md § C1 (Design D1/D2/D3).

schema.description: Schema discriminator — always 'sizing-object'. Enables kind-first schema matching.

intent.description: The PM ask, verbatim. Not paraphrased or summarized — the raw framing the sizing lobby routed on.

appetite.description: The Shape-Up BUDGET the PM MAY state for this work — never collected before the size is delivered, and never a precondition for this sizing-object to validate (see `required`, which no longer names this field). When the PM does volunteer one, it is a FIXED BUDGET set up front, NOT a reason to defer scope and NOT 'appetite-based OOS' (which coordinator doctrine bans — see coordinator/docs/wiki/implementation-standards-by-domain.md § Cross-cutting standards: 'OOS framing must be architectural, not appetite-based'). Appetite bounds how much time/effort is worth spending; it never justifies cutting a correctness/integrity requirement out of scope.

estimate.description: Coarse routing-only size estimate. Distinct from the committed plan-body LoE (two-altitude model, D1.3): this estimate exists to pick which room (route) the work enters, not to bind the eventual plan's effort accounting.

tshirt.description: T-shirt size estimate. Reuses the existing loe.tshirt enum and weights verbatim (XS=1, S=2, M=4, L=8, XL=16, XXL=32) — see coordinator/schemas/completion-entry.schema.json loe.tshirt. Do not invent a parallel scale.

provisional.description: Always true. Marks this tshirt value as a COARSE, revisable ROUTING estimate (which room to enter) — never the committed plan-body LoE. A plan authored downstream re-estimates independently; this field is not inherited as authoritative effort.

route.description: The room this sizing routes the work into: dispatch=small enough to execute directly, no artifact; spec-dispatch=small enough for a light plan artifact then dispatch, no Opus plan review; shape=problem not yet converged, needs /shape first; plan=decision-weight work needing coordinator:plan; roadmap=initiative-scale, needs roadmap-planning; pm-decision=initiative-scale and not a room by itself — the engine picks no room and the PM chooses among four exits (see `xl_exit`); goal-setting=initiative-scale beyond a single roadmap — routes to the PM-gated goal-setting ceremony.

detents.description: Boundary detents crossed or acknowledged while sizing this work — the discrete stops the sizing lobby snapped to (e.g. appetite/estimate divergence, route-boundary crossing) before landing on the final route. Empty array when no boundary was crossed. `premise_unproven` and `premise_not_applicable` are ADVISORY: they mirror the `premise.provenance` value (see the `premise` object) into a queryable detent, but never change the resolved `route` and never populate `xl_exit`.

fork.description: Null unless appetite and estimate diverge (estimate's implied size exceeds or undershoots the appetite budget). When set, this is UNRESOLVED BY CONSTRUCTION — the sizing skill surfaces the fork to the PM, it never auto-resolves it. cut_to_fit=trim scope to fit the existing appetite; raise_appetite=the PM increases the budget instead.

xl_exit.description: The PM's recorded choice among the four XL exits when `route` is `pm-decision`. The engine NEVER sets this — it always emits `null`, exactly as it does for `fork`. `null` is a legitimate open state meaning the PM has not chosen yet; it NEVER means the multi-session exit was accepted by default. Each value has a stated precondition: split=the ask decomposes into >=2 pieces that ship independently, each with its own acceptance criteria and no piece depending on an unshipped sibling's contract; shape=the job-to-be-done is not stated, or the EM cannot falsifiably restate the problem in the PM's vocabulary; roadmap=the work spans >=2 named workstreams, or carries (or needs) an initiative/goal FK — a programme of plans, not one plan; accept_multi_session=none of the other three preconditions hold and the PM has explicitly assented — writing this value IS that record.

scout_evidence.description: Pointers to cartography/scout output that informed this sizing (file paths, wiki citations, prior-art references). Empty array when no scout ran.

surfaced_to_pm.description: Direction-class items the sizing surfaced to the PM but deliberately did NOT decide. Distinct from `fork` and `xl_exit`, which are the two structured halts the lobby computes for itself: this array is for everything else the EM noticed while sizing that is the PM's call — a standing ruling the new evidence bears on, a product-direction question the work would force, an external-facing consequence. NEGATIVE SPEC: this is never a record of a decision. An entry stays listed until it is resolved in its own artifact (a decision record, a PM ruling, a downstream plan); resolving it by editing the sizing-object is the failure this field exists to prevent. Once resolved, the PM's reasoning moves to `pm_resolution`. Empty array when nothing was surfaced. Exists because the alternative — a YAML comment — is invisible to any query over state/sizings/, which is how a surfaced item silently becomes a forgotten one.

item.description: The direction-class question itself, stated so a reader who was not in the session can act on it. Not a topic label.

why_not_decided.description: Why the EM did not settle this while sizing — e.g. a standing PM ruling this evidence bears on but does not overturn, product direction, an irreversible/external action, or a genuine no-correct-answer tradeoff. 'Not now' is not a reason; if the only reason is cost, it is break-class work to be fixed, not a direction-class item to be surfaced.

prior_ruling.description: Optional pointer to the existing decision, ruling, or audit entry this item bears on (file:line, DR-id, or artifact path). Present when the item revisits settled ground rather than opening new ground — its absence means no prior ruling was found, not that none exists.

pm_resolution.description: The PM's recorded answer once they have resolved this sizing's open questions — the counterpart to `surfaced_to_pm`, which holds what is still open. Free-form string values by design: what a PM settles at a sizing varies (which fork, which XL exit, where an artifact should live), and a closed property list would push the next unanticipated decision back into an ad-hoc key or a comment. NEGATIVE SPEC: `fork` and `xl_exit` remain the AUTHORITATIVE machine-readable record of those two choices — an entry here carries the PM's REASONING, never a substitute value, and must not contradict them. Omit entirely when nothing has been resolved; an empty object is not a resolution.

decided_on.description: Date the PM actually decided (YYYY-MM-DD), not the date the sizing was authored.

additionalProperties.description: One resolved question, keyed by what it resolved (e.g. `appetite_fork`, `xl_exit`, `wiki_home`). Value states the choice AND the reasoning, so a later reader need not reconstruct why.

status.description: Sizing-object lifecycle. draft=intent captured, not yet estimated; sized=estimate+appetite set, fork may be outstanding; routed=route chosen and handed off (fork, if any, resolved); superseded=replaced by a later sizing for the same intent.

superseded_note.description: Present only when `status` is `superseded`. Records WHY this sizing-object was superseded — the verification that invalidated it, the root cause, and where the live surface moved to. Distinct from `pm_resolution`: this is EM-observed process history about the sizing-object's own lifecycle, not the PM's decision reasoning, and must not be folded into `pm_resolution`.

premise.description: Whether the premise this sizing is built on was ever actually verified, before structure gets built on top of a guess. ADVISORY ONLY — the detent this can produce downstream (`sizing_assemble`'s `premise_unproven`, engine-side) NEVER blocks a route; it never changes the resolved `route` and never populates `xl_exit`. Discharge is by CITING THE EXECUTED EVIDENCE INLINE in the `evidence` field below — a file:line, test name, command output, or read location the author actually looked at — NEVER by producing a separate spike-result record; a premise question is answered in place, not spun into its own artifact. `provenance`: executed=the premise was verified by actually running/reproducing it; read=the premise rests on reading code/docs/a prior record, not on execution; not-applicable=this ask has no premise to verify (state the reason in `evidence`); unrecorded=migration-only, meaning this record predates this field and its premise provenance was never captured. DR-068 (docs/decisions/DR-068-commit-time-coverage-gate-scoped-shift-left-ambient-handoff-flat-fallback-advisory.md) is the standing precedent for this advisory-not-blocking shape — that ruling made the same call for the commit-time DAG verdict, and this field follows the same house answer rather than inventing a new one.

provenance.description: executed=verified by actually running/reproducing it; read=rests on reading code/docs/a prior record, not execution; not-applicable=this ask has no premise to verify; unrecorded=migration-only, the record predates this field.

evidence.description: The executed evidence cited inline (file:line, test name, command output, or read location) — or, when `provenance` is `not-applicable`, why. Required for every `provenance` value except `unrecorded`.

spike_verdict.description: Path to the spike-verdict record produced by `coordinator:spike` when a spike upgraded this sizing's premise from `read` to `executed`. NEGATIVE SPEC: never substitutes for `evidence` — `evidence` stays required for every provenance value except `unrecorded`, and the inline citation remains the discharge (see this object's own "answered in place, not spun into its own artifact" rule). `spike_verdict` is the structured pointer to the ceremony record; `evidence` is still what a reader reads. Absent when no spike ran.

spike_amendments.description: BINDING SCOPE for the downstream plan — the discharged routing intent a `coordinator:spike` produced, recorded where the plan-author will read it. NEGATIVE SPEC: not a substitute for the downstream plan's own scope or chunking, and not a place to record spike findings that changed nothing — an entry exists because it re-specs something. Omit entirely when no spike ran; an empty array is not an amendment set.

scope.description: What this amendment binds: the named sub-piece of the ask it re-specs, or `cross-cutting` for one that binds the whole. Always a string, even when the underlying identifier is numeric.

amendment.description: The binding routing intent the spike produced for this scope: what the spike's executed evidence changed about how this work must be planned.
